There is a little needy monster living in my plant pot, it keeps screaming for chips and beer. Someone makes a mess in my apartment when I sleep. Summary: This really has very little to do with unemployment and more of a interactive story of some massive massive massive mental health problems. Gameplay: There honestly there isn't much you can do. Like you are given a few task (clean x dishes as example) but outside of those few things. There is not a lot of gameplay. It should be noted a number of times it ask you to do something and there isn't really any clue. When to feed the worm, it is asking you to feed it chips. Story: It really isnt' that good. Ignoring how it has virtually nothing to do with unemployment. The game is basically about some guy who has some seriously mental health issues where flies talk to him in his sleep. It doesn't seem like choices don't really matter. Like as far as I can tell there is no way to really change the story but the tail end and maybe 1 other part. Like outside very exact moments which are extremely far and few between you are on for the ride.

Game is alright but I kinda wish there was more to it. Like even when I was unemployed I went outside and sometimes took walks in the park. While I can't say the game mechanics are great I would say the pixel art is on point and the game doesn't seem to have any bugs. The story is mildly interesting but it ends pretty abruptly. While it makes a great conversation piece as people tend to snicker whenever I say I played Unemployment Simulator 2018 I can't really recommend it as I find it doesn't have enough going for it. The gameplay could be improved by adding more sim elements like food with differing effects. We already have coffee that speeds you up so why not a homecooked meal that slowers dopamine loss? Also maybe eating unhealthy gives you good dopamine but damages your health a bit and doesn't really fill your hunger depending on the food. Something about the game looked appealing, in a light maybe funny kinda way. And It was a good pick, I thought "Eh, maybe on sale" and ignored it. Admittedly I bought it drunk recently to 'celebrate' my cousin's recent decision to quit his job, I bought it for both of us. So when he went to bed drunk the next night early I thought 'Why not?'. The music is very well done. Bravo for that alone, it kept my head there the whole time. I appreciate good sound choices. The art and lightly changing scenery was also pleasant (and that's saying something considering the size of the playable area). But it's unique flavor of the game that I appreciated most. I'm content to have done this late at night while drinking and taken 2 days to do it. It is a great "I really should be going to bed" game. I'm gonna grab the rest of the achievements before I shelve it. But It was a reflection of what little gem games can be to the right person.

Unemployment Simulator 2018 is an unconventional life simulation that explores a topic rarely addressed in games: the emotional and practical reality of living without a job. Developed by Samuel Lehikoinen and published by turbolento publishing, the game places players in the role of an unemployed individual struggling to maintain a sense of purpose while confined to a modest apartment. Drawing inspiration from the developer's personal experiences, it offers a grounded and often uncomfortable look at everyday survival, replacing traditional action and adventure with the challenges of managing both physical needs and mental well-being. Its willingness to tackle a realistic and sensitive subject immediately sets it apart from more conventional simulators. Instead of focusing on wealth, career progression, or building an empire, the gameplay centers on simply making it through each day. Players must carefully balance hunger, hygiene, energy, boredom, and emotional stability while stretching limited resources. Everyday tasks such as preparing meals, cleaning the apartment, brushing teeth, filling out job applications, or finding something entertaining become meaningful objectives. One of the game's more distinctive systems revolves around managing dopamine, encouraging players to seek healthy forms of stimulation to avoid sinking further into depression and apathy. These mechanics successfully transform routine activities into engaging survival elements while emphasizing how difficult ordinary responsibilities can become under prolonged stress. The narrative gradually unfolds through a combination of daily life and surreal dream sequences. Every night offers a temporary escape from reality as the protagonist imagines different versions of life, from fulfilling careers to extraordinary adventures. These dream segments provide a welcome contrast to the repetitive nature of daily survival while also highlighting the gap between hopes and reality. Rather than relying on dramatic plot twists, the story builds emotional weight through subtle moments, making the player's small victories feel surprisingly rewarding. Visually, the game embraces a retro-inspired pixel art style that complements its intimate setting. Although the environment remains largely confined to a single apartment, thoughtful environmental details prevent it from feeling lifeless. The soundtrack enhances the atmosphere with music that alternates between reflective, melancholic, and occasionally uplifting tones, reinforcing both the loneliness and the quiet optimism that define the experience. The combination of simple visuals and effective audio design creates a believable world that supports the game's emotional themes. Another notable strength is its balance between serious storytelling and dark humor. The writing recognizes that humor often emerges during difficult situations, allowing awkward and absurd moments to coexist naturally with themes of depression, financial hardship, and isolation. Mature content, including references to alcohol consumption, nudity, and mental health struggles, is incorporated to support the realism of the narrative rather than simply to provoke. This gives the game a level of authenticity that feels respectful toward the subject matter while remaining entertaining. The deliberate pacing will not appeal to everyone. Players expecting constant excitement or rapid progression may find the repetitive routines demanding, as much of the experience involves maintaining daily habits and carefully managing limited resources. However, this repetition serves the central message well, illustrating the monotony and emotional exhaustion that can accompany long-term unemployment. The game succeeds because it commits fully to its premise rather than simplifying the experience into a traditional management simulator. Overall, Unemployment Simulator 2018 delivers a surprisingly thoughtful and emotionally engaging experience that stands out through its originality and honesty. By combining survival mechanics, psychological storytelling, life simulation, and understated humor, it offers a perspective rarely explored in interactive entertainment. Although its slow pace and mature themes may limit its audience, those interested in narrative-driven simulations with meaningful social commentary will likely appreciate its unique approach. It is an ambitious indie title that transforms ordinary life into a compelling survival experience. Rating: 8/10
